**The two chambers as two grids.** Queen's Chamber (the ka's room, misnamed by medieval Arabs): on the axis over the natural knoll, floor at 21.2 m ≈ H/7 (20.9), shafts sealed at both ends, niche for the statue. Built to stay. King's Chamber: off-axis ~11 m south, floor at 43.0 m where the horizontal section has exactly half the base area, h = H(1 − 1/√2) = 42.9 m; shafts open to the pole and Orion. The Egyptian sevenths grid catches the Queen's Chamber tightly and the King's loosely; √2 the reverse. Two grids, each owning different corners.

The coffer in the King's Chamber has a sliding groove on three sides and three pin holes in its rim; its lid has never been found and no lid fragments are recorded in the chamber or passages. Khafre's coffer lid lies unbroken on the floor of his burial chamber. In the Grotto, at the edge of a hollow dug by treasure hunters after Ma'mun, lies a broken granite fragment with two worked surfaces at right angles and parts of two large drilled holes (Edgar 1910). Petrie recovered a worked granite block from the Descending Passage with a four-inch drill hole through it; the Edgars note two further large granite pieces in the passages, each with a pair of drill holes. **Breath.** Prevailing north wind on the north face, lee suction on the south: ~80 Pa across 120 m of 20 cm duct gives a ~2.5 m/s draft through the King's Chamber. Sun on the south casing adds a solar-chimney term (~8 Pa, ~0.8 m/s), reversing at night. In from the north (imperishable stars), out to the south (Orion). The stela wish "may he breathe the sweet breath of the north wind" arrives through the north shaft.

**Drying.** Six-million-tonne thermal mass holds the King's Chamber at ~20 °C year round. The only ventilated chamber in any Old Kingdom pyramid, set high in dry masonry. Control: the Queen's Chamber (lower, shafts never opened) carries a salt crust up to ~1 cm; the King's Chamber almost none. Same rock, same visitors; the ventilated room stayed dry.

**Khufu's secret, by the cube.** Not an object. He moved himself off the body corner: identity in the load-bearing stone, survival in other people's mouths (every private tomb's formula begins "an offering which the king gives"; offerings reverted down the plateau through his), the two trusted men on either side, the mother at the fixed point, the body in a nameless box by his dynasty's custom. Inverse cell left empty.
